# Configuration

<!-- Generated by `uv run python -m keryx.config.reference`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting Keryx reads, by the name you set it under, and by its title: what the Mac app
calls it. The usual way to set them is `uv run keryx setup` (a wizard that asks only for
what is missing) or `uv run keryx config set KEY VALUE`; `uv run keryx config list` shows
each one with where its value came from.

**Where they live.** `KERYX_HOME` (default `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/keryx`, which is
`~/.config/keryx`, on Linux and macOS alike) holds `config.toml` for the plain settings and
`secrets.toml` for the credentials, both readable by you alone. A secret is never put on a
command line: `keryx config set KEY --stdin` reads it from standard input, and
`--from-env VAR` from a variable. The PIN is not in either file: it lives beside them in
`KERYX_HOME/pin`, written once (see `SECURITY.md`). Keep that directory out of a
dotfiles repository. What Keryx keeps is in `DATA_DIR`, `STATE_DIR` and `CACHE_DIR`, the
XDG data, state and cache directories below.

**Which value wins**, first to last: the process environment (a systemd `Environment=`,
say), `secrets.toml`, `config.toml`, and the default below. Nothing is read from the
working directory: an install that still has a `.env` there, or its files in `~/.jarvis`,
moves them with `keryx migrate`, and `keryx serve` refuses to start until it has.

**What the running service may change.** Keryx can change some of its own settings — the
voice model's `set_config` tool, or a subagent running `keryx config set` in a task — and
only those marked *yes* below, until you say otherwise with `keryx config unlock KEY` or
`keryx config lock KEY`. The ones marked *never* are protected: every credential, and
every setting that is a line of defence (who may call, the approval allowlist, filing
issues in public, spending caps, deletion, the network, the debug switches). Nothing unlocks them.

**In the Mac app** most settings are on the Configuration screen's seven tabs, and each
section below names its own:
General, Voice, Agents, Phone, Approvals, Integrations, System.
The voice's models and this machine's model servers are on screens of their own instead:
the Voice screen and the Local Models screen.
Each is the one place its settings are changed, and Configuration's search still finds
them and takes you there.
A tab opens on its *key* settings — what you set to get a first call working, or change
from time to time, how long your calls and tasks are kept and how many tasks a day may
run included — and keeps the rest under an *Advanced* disclosure: tuning and internals,
such as turn-detection numbers, server addresses, ports, timeouts, per-task caps, folders,
unit names, the log level and the debug switches.

## Voice

In the Mac app: the Voice tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key | key | (secret) | never | OpenAI API key with Realtime access: the voice, unless `VOICE_BASE_URL` names a server of your own, and the voice model's `web_search`. |
| `ASSISTANT_NAME` | Assistant name | key | `Lyra` | yes | What the assistant on the phone is called: the name it answers to and introduces itself by. Lyra and Jarvis each bring a voice of their own; any other name — letters, spaces, apostrophes and hyphens, up to 32 — speaks in `OPENAI_VOICE`, or `marin`. |
| `TRANSCRIPTION_LANGUAGE` | Transcription language | key | `` | yes | The language you speak on a call, as an ISO-639-1 code (`en`, `de`, `fr`), for the call log's transcription — which `recall` and the memory read. Empty lets the transcriber guess each turn. The voice model itself hears the audio either way. |
| `CLOCK_FORMAT` | Clock format | key | `24h` | yes | How the voice prompt writes the time of day (`14:05` or `2:05 PM`), and so how the assistant tends to say it. |
| `VOICE_PIPELINE` | Voice pipeline | advanced |  | never | How a call's voice is built: `speech-to-speech`, one model that hears and speaks (OpenAI, or a Realtime server elsewhere), or `three-model`, speech-to-text, an LLM and text-to-speech (the voice here). Blank is the only one `VOICE_MODE` offers today; one it does not offer is refused. |
| `OPENAI_WEB_SEARCH_MODEL` | Web search model | advanced | `gpt-6-luna` | no | Answers the voice model's own `web_search` tool, through the Responses API (the Realtime API has no hosted search tool). |

## OpenAI Realtime tuning

In the Mac app: the Voice tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` | Transcription model | advanced | `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` | no | Transcribes what the caller says, for the call log, on OpenAI; a voice of your own transcribes with its own speech-to-text. |
| `VAD_MODE` | Turn detection | advanced | `semantic` | yes | How the assistant decides you have finished: `semantic` waits on whether the sentence sounds finished, so a pause to think does not cut you off; `server` is a plain silence timer of `VAD_SILENCE_MS`. |
| `VAD_EAGERNESS` | Reply eagerness | advanced | `medium` | yes | Semantic mode only: `low` waits longest, `high` jumps in soonest, `auto` is `medium`. |
| `VAD_SILENCE_MS` | Silence to end a turn (ms) | advanced | `1200` | yes | Server mode only: the silence, in milliseconds, that ends a turn. |
| `VAD_THRESHOLD` | Speech threshold | advanced | `0.5` | yes | Server mode only: how loud counts as speech (0 to 1). |
| `VAD_PREFIX_MS` | Audio before speech (ms) | advanced | `300` | yes | Server mode only: audio kept from before speech was detected, so the first syllable is not clipped. |
| `NOISE_REDUCTION` | Noise reduction | advanced | `auto` | yes | Background-noise suppression on what the model hears; `auto` picks `near_field` for a phone and `far_field` for a microphone across the room. Mostly about barge-in: noise mistaken for speech is noise that cuts the assistant off. |

## Voice models

In the Mac app: the Voice screen.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL` | Realtime model | key | `gpt-realtime-2.1` | no | The realtime speech-to-speech model a call runs on, on OpenAI. A voice server elsewhere is sent it too (as `?model=`); the voice pipeline here never is. |
| `OPENAI_VOICE` | Assistant voice | key | `` | yes | The Realtime voice the assistant speaks in. Empty is the assistant's own (`ASSISTANT_NAME`); a voice the key's organization may not use makes every call fail to open. Sent to OpenAI only, and for one release to a voice server elsewhere that has no `VOICE_SERVER_VOICE`. |
| `VOICE_MODE` | Where the voice runs | key |  | never | Where a call's voice runs: `openai` is OpenAI Realtime, `here` the speech pipeline on this machine (`VOICE_SERVER_*`), `server` a Realtime server elsewhere (`VOICE_BASE_URL`). Blank is worked out from `VOICE_BASE_URL`, as it was before this was a setting: blank is OpenAI, this machine's voice port is here, any other address a server. |
| `VOICE_BASE_URL` | Voice server URL | key |  | never | A voice server of your own that speaks the OpenAI Realtime protocol, as its `…/v1` address (`http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1` is the one `keryx setup` installs). Blank is OpenAI. |
| `VOICE_API_KEY` | Voice server API key | key | (secret) | never | The Bearer key for that voice server, when it checks one. |
| `VOICE_SERVER_STT` | Speech-to-text model | key | `parakeet-tdt` | no | How the local voice server hears: speech-to-speech's `--stt` (`parakeet-tdt`, `whisper`, …). |
| `VOICE_LLM` | Voice LLM | key | `shared` | never | Where the words of a voice running here come from: `shared` is the local agent's model on its server, `here` a model of the voice's own (`VOICE_LLM_MODEL`) on a server of its own on this machine, `remote` a server elsewhere (`VOICE_LLM_BASE_URL`) — a box of yours, or a cloud's Responses API. |
| `VOICE_LLM_MODEL` | Voice LLM model | key |  | no | The voice LLM's model. With `VOICE_LLM=here`, a name from `keryx models list` or a GGUF file's path, served under that name; with `remote`, the server's own name for it. Not read while the voice LLM is shared. |
| `VOICE_LLM_BASE_URL` | Voice LLM server URL | key |  | never | With `VOICE_LLM=remote`, the server the voice's words go to, as its `…/v1` address (`https://api.openai.com/v1` for OpenAI's). |
| `VOICE_LLM_API_KEY` | Voice LLM API key | key | (secret) | never | The Bearer key for that server, when it checks one. Blank sends `OPENAI_API_KEY` only when the address is OpenAI's own, and no key of yours anywhere else. |
| `VOICE_SERVER_TTS` | Text-to-speech model | key | `kokoro` | no | How the local voice server speaks: speech-to-speech's `--tts` (`kokoro`, `qwen3`, …). |
| `VOICE_SERVER_VOICE` | Kokoro voice | key | `af_heart` | no | The Kokoro voice the local voice server speaks in (`af_heart`, `bm_george`, …; `keryx models list` shows them). A voice server elsewhere is sent it too, once it is set. |
| `VOICE_SERVER_ARGS` | Extra voice server flags | advanced | `` | never | More flags for `speech-to-speech serve`, as a command line — a smaller speech model (`--stt_model_name openai/whisper-base`), a TTS speed. Never a key: it is on argv. |

## Coding agents

In the Mac app: the Agents tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_BACKEND` | Default agent | key | `claude` | yes | The coding agent a task runs on when nobody names one out loud. The running service may switch it only among `AGENTS_ENABLED`. |
| `AGENTS_ENABLED` | Enabled agents | key |  | no | Every agent a task may be sent to, comma-separated; blank is `AGENT_BACKEND` alone. `keryx serve` refuses a default that is not in here. |
| `SUBAGENT_TIMEOUT_S` | Time limit per task (seconds) | advanced | `10800` | yes | The longest one subagent run may take, on any agent, in seconds; 0 is no limit. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key | key | (secret) | never | Claude, paid per token. Set, it wins over the subscription. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | Claude subscription token | key | (secret) | never | Claude on your subscription, for a machine with no browser: the token `claude setup-token` prints. Blank uses the stored `claude` login. |
| `CLAUDE_MODEL` | Claude model | key | `claude-opus-5-5` | yes | The model a Claude task runs on when none is named. |
| `SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS` | Turns per task | advanced | `200` | no | Agent turns one Claude task may take. |
| `SUBAGENT_MAX_BUDGET_USD` | Budget per task (USD) | advanced | `10` | never | Dollars one Claude task may spend: a runaway cap. On a subscription it is the SDK's estimate of what the task would have cost, not a charge. |
| `CODEX_API_KEY` | Codex API key | key | (secret) | never | Codex, paid per token. Keryx logs in with it once, into its own `CODEX_HOME`; `OPENAI_API_KEY` is never used for Codex. |
| `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Codex subscription token | key | (secret) | never | Codex on your ChatGPT plan, for a machine with no browser. Blank uses the stored `codex login`. |
| `CODEX_MODEL` | Codex model | key |  | yes | The model a Codex task runs on; blank is Codex's own default. |

## Local agent

In the Mac app: the Agents tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LOCAL_AGENT_BASE_URL` | Local agent server URL | advanced |  | never | An inference server for the `local` agent — Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio — as `http://gpu-box:11434` or its `…/v1` address. Blank is no local agent. |
| `LOCAL_AGENT_API_KEY` | Local agent API key | advanced | (secret) | never | The Bearer key for that server, when it checks one. The owner's Anthropic and OpenAI credentials are never sent there. |
| `LOCAL_AGENT_MODEL` | Local agent model | key |  | yes | The model a `local` task runs on, by the server's own name for it. |
| `LOCAL_AGENT_API` | Local agent harness | advanced | `anthropic-messages` | yes | Which harness drives the local model: `anthropic-messages` runs it inside Claude Code, `openai-responses` inside Codex. The server must speak that API. |

## Owner, callers and PIN

In the Mac app: the General tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OWNER_NAME` | Your name | key |  | no | What the assistant calls you in the prompts it is handed; blank is "the owner". Only a name: the rest of what it knows about you is its memory. |
| `ALLOWED_CALLERS` | Your phone numbers | key |  | never | Your phone numbers in E.164 (`+15551234567`), comma-separated. Every other caller is refused. This is the handsets one person picks up, not a guest list: a call Keryx places to any of them reached you. |
| `OWNER_NUMBER` | Number to ring first | key |  | never | Which of your numbers Keryx rings first; blank is the first of `ALLOWED_CALLERS`. |
| `KERYX_PIN` | Phone PIN | key | (secret) | never | The phone PIN: 6 to 8 digits, asked for before anything is dispatched from a call. Not kept in the configuration files: it lives in `KERYX_HOME/pin`, written once by `keryx setup` or by the first call, and this variable, set in the environment, overrides that file. With no PIN anywhere nothing of yours is read out on the phone and every dispatch is refused. |
| `PIN_FAILURE_LIMIT` | Wrong PINs before lockout | advanced | `10` | never | Wrong PINs, counted across every call, before PIN entry locks for everyone — the right PIN included. |
| `PIN_FAILURE_WINDOW_HOURS` | Wrong PINs remembered (hours) | advanced | `24` | never | How long a wrong PIN is remembered. |
| `PIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES` | Lockout length (minutes) | advanced | `60` | never | How long PIN entry stays locked once the limit is reached. |
| `BRIEFING_BEFORE_PIN` | Briefing before the PIN | key | `true` | never | Whether a call is handed its standing briefing — unreported results, the memory, project names, briefs, skills — before the PIN. The PIN is the line between reading and acting; off means nothing of yours is said until it is given. Does nothing until a PIN exists. |

## Phone

In the Mac app: the Phone tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` | Twilio account SID | key |  | no | Your Twilio account SID (`AC…`). |
| `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | Twilio auth token | key | (secret) | never | Your Twilio auth token. |
| `TWILIO_NUMBER` | Twilio number | key |  | no | The Twilio number Keryx answers and calls from, in E.164. |
| `SMS_ENABLED` | Text messages (SMS) | key | `false` | never | Whether Keryx may text at all. Off: many Twilio accounts cannot send SMS in their region, and Slack is the written channel. Outbound calls are unaffected. |

| `CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL` | Cloudflare tunnel | advanced | `keryx` | never | The Cloudflare tunnel the service scripts run (`scripts/dev.sh`, `scripts/install-systemd.sh`). |
| `HOST` | Phone server address | advanced | `127.0.0.1` | never | The address the phone server binds. |
| `PORT` | Phone server port | advanced | `8080` | never | The port the phone server binds. |

## Google

In the Mac app: the Integrations tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` | OAuth client ID | key |  | no | The Google OAuth client id. Blank: read from `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRETS_FILE`. |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | OAuth client secret | key | (secret) | never | The Google OAuth client secret, with the id above. |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRETS_FILE` | OAuth client file | advanced |  | no | The OAuth client JSON the Google Cloud console downloads (desktop or web shape). Blank: `KERYX_HOME/google_client_secret.json`, where `keryx setup` puts it. |
| `USER_GOOGLE_EMAIL` | Google account | key |  | no | The Google account agents act as; `keryx setup` fills it in from the sign-in. |
| `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_MCP` | Workspace MCP server | key | `false` | no | Give every subagent the workspace-mcp server (send mail, manage the calendar). Needed for Codex, which has no claude.ai connectors; Claude already has them. |

## Projects and skills

In the Mac app: the Integrations tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PROJECTS` | Other projects | key |  | no | Spoken project names for repositories outside `PROJECTS_ROOT`, as `{"name": "/path"}`. |
| `PROJECTS_ROOT` | Projects folder | key | `~/projects` | no | Where a task with no project starts; each subdirectory is a project you can name. Never created: without it, such a task starts in `DATA_DIR/workspace`. |
| `SKILLS_DIR` | Skills folder | advanced | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills` (`~/.claude/skills`) | never | Where the Claude CLI keeps its skills; listed in the voice prompt so the assistant knows what the subagents are good at. |
| `KERYX_CHECKOUT` | Keryx checkout | advanced |  | no | The Keryx repository on this machine, which a subagent reads when it reports a problem with Keryx. Unset: the checkout Keryx runs from, when it runs from one. |
| `ISSUE_REPORTING` | GitHub issue reports | key | `false` | never | Whether a bug or a feature request for Keryx, said on a call, may be filed as a GitHub issue by a subagent, with `gh`. `keryx setup` asks; only you can turn it on. |
| `ISSUE_REPO` | Issue repository | advanced | `wak31415/keryx` | never | The GitHub repository (`owner/name`) those issues are filed on. |

## The approval bridge

In the Mac app: the Approvals tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `APPROVALS_ENABLED` | Approval calls | key | `true` | never | Whether a Claude Code prompt left unanswered on your screen may become a call. The hook is installed separately (`scripts/install-claude-hook.sh`). |
| `APPROVAL_ESCALATE_SECONDS` | Ring after (seconds) | advanced | `300` | no | How long a prompt waits on screen before Keryx rings about it. |
| `APPROVAL_CALL_WINDOW_SECONDS` | Answer window (seconds) | advanced | `240` | no | How long the hook keeps waiting after that. The two together are the longest the hook blocks; its `timeout` in `~/.claude/settings.json` must exceed their sum. |
| `APPROVAL_MAX_PER_HOUR` | Maximum calls per hour | advanced | `4` | no | Approval calls per hour, however many prompts pile up. |
| `APPROVAL_QUIET_HOURS` | Quiet hours | key |  | yes | `HH:MM-HH:MM` in which it never rings (may cross midnight), in the host's time. |
| `APPROVAL_BASH_ALLOW` | Allowed commands | advanced | `git push,git commit` | never | The only shell commands a keypad digit may ever run, matched word for word; only `git push` and `git commit` may carry arguments (`keryx/approvals/policy.py`). This allowlist is the primary control: widening it widens exactly what a phone keypad can execute. |
| `APPROVAL_ROOTS` | Writable folders | advanced |  | never | Where a file may be written by phone approval; blank is `PROJECTS_ROOT` plus every project in `PROJECTS`. |

## Limits and retention

In the Mac app: the System tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS` | Tasks at once | advanced | `3` | yes | Subagents running at once; the rest queue. |
| `DISPATCH_WAIT_MAX_SECONDS` | Inline answer wait (seconds) | advanced | `25` | no | How long a call waits for a short task to answer inline. |
| `LOCAL_SILENCE_TIMEOUT` | Local session timeout (seconds) | advanced | `30` | yes | Seconds of silence that end a local session; 0 never does. |
| `MAX_CALL_SECONDS` | Maximum call length (seconds) | advanced | `1800` | yes | The longest a phone call may run; Keryx wraps up 30 s before. 0 is no limit. |
| `MAX_PHONE_SESSIONS` | Phone calls at once | advanced | `2` | no | Phone calls open at once, each one a realtime session being paid for; another hears that the line is busy. |
| `DAILY_TASK_CAP` | Tasks per day | key | `50` | never | Tasks dispatched per day. |
| `TRANSCRIPT_RETENTION_DAYS` | Keep transcripts for (days) | key | `0` | never | Delete call transcripts older than this many days; 0 keeps everything. |
| `TASK_RETENTION_DAYS` | Keep finished tasks for (days) | key | `0` | never | Delete finished tasks older than this; 0 keeps everything. A result you have not been told about is never deleted. |

## Service, storage and logging

In the Mac app: the System tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DATA_DIR` | Data folder | advanced | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/keryx` (`~/.local/share/keryx`) | never | Where tasks, transcripts, memory and sign-in tokens are kept, owner-only (0700, files 0600). |
| `STATE_DIR` | State folder | advanced | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/keryx` (`~/.local/state/keryx`) | never | Where the logs, the restart record and the approval bridge's socket are kept, owner-only. |
| `CACHE_DIR` | Cache folder | advanced | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/keryx` (`~/.cache/keryx`) | never | Where what can be downloaded again is kept. |
| `SERVICE_MANAGER` | Service manager | advanced | `auto` | never | What `keryx restart` asks to restart this process: `auto` is systemd or launchd, but only for a process actually running under it; `none` refuses. |
| `SERVICE_UNIT` | Service unit or label | advanced |  | never | The systemd unit or launchd label; blank is the installed default (`keryx.service`, `dev.keryx.agent`). |
| `REPORT_SECRET` | Report link secret | advanced | (secret) | never | Signs the `/reports/{id}` links texted to you; blank generates one into `DATA_DIR/report_secret`. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | Log level | advanced | `INFO` | yes | How much `STATE_DIR/logs/keryx.log` says. |

## Development switches

In the Mac app: the System tab.

| Setting | Title | In the app | Default | Service may change | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DEBUG_SKIP_TWILIO_VALIDATION` | Skip Twilio signatures | advanced | `false` | never | Skip Twilio's request signatures, for a machine nothing outside can reach. `keryx serve` refuses the phone with it on behind a `PUBLIC_HOST`. |
| `DEMO_MODE` | Demo mode | advanced | `false` | never | Try the phone before a coding agent is set up: calls, the PIN and call-backs are real, and every task comes back after a moment with a sample answer that says it was a demo. No agent runs and no agent tokens are spent. `keryx serve --demo` turns it on for one run. |
